title: API Gateway from Scratch with Plugin Architecture
problem: Modern microservice topologies require centralized networking ingress points to enforce cross-cutting concerns including transport-level security, authentication verification, request rate limiting, and dynamic traffic routing without duplicating boilerplate across individual services. Operating reverse proxies under sustained traffic introduces challenging failure modes such as connection pool exhaustion, file descriptor leaks, thread contention, and dropped requests during configuration changes. An engineered API gateway addresses these operational challenges by implementing tuned socket pooling, lock-free route table hot-reloading, active upstream health checking with automated failover, and an extensible pipeline for custom middleware plugins.
use_cases: Edge ingress routing and token authentication for heterogeneous microservice clusters
Dynamic traffic shifting and canary release management across upstream service versions
Centralized rate limiting and telemetry metering for external partner API access
hard_parts: Eliminating socket exhaustion and TIME_WAIT saturation under high concurrency through tuned connection reuse and response body drain policies
Executing zero-downtime route table hot-reloading via atomic pointer swapping without dropping in-flight client requests
Minimizing garbage collection pause overhead in the proxy data path by recycling byte buffers with sync pools
Mitigating upstream server flapping through hysteresis counters in active background health check loops
screener_signals: Standalone Go codebase implementing custom reverse proxying without high-level gateway frameworks
Concurrency-safe route hot-reloading demonstrated under active automated load without connection drops
Anti-fake verification script validating dynamic upstream registration and live header transformation

components.name: Proxy Core Engine
components.purpose: Intercepts client HTTP requests, recycles byte buffers using sync pools, and forwards requests via tuned HTTP transports

components.name: Atomic Route Registry
components.purpose: Stores dynamic routing rules using atomic pointers to allow lock-free hot-reloading via an Admin REST API

components.name: Middleware Plugin Pipeline
components.purpose: Executes sequential plugin stages including authentication token validation, sliding window rate limiting, and header transformation

components.name: Upstream Health Balancer
components.purpose: Performs background health checks every second and distributes traffic across healthy upstreams via weighted round-robin

components.name: Metrics & Telemetry Exporter
components.purpose: Exposes standard Prometheus metrics tracking request durations, active connections, and upstream error statuses

components.name: Upstream Cluster Simulator
components.purpose: Runs multi-instance backend mock services with configurable chaos endpoints for failover validation

architecture.data_flow: Client HTTP requests reach the Go proxy engine; the router reads an atomic snapshot of current routes; the request traverses the middleware plugin chain (Auth -> RateLimiter -> HeaderMutator); the load balancer selects an active upstream replica from healthy nodes; the request is forwarded via pooled TCP connections; upstream response streams back to the client while Prometheus metrics increment.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Rate limiting plugin returns HTTP 429 when client exceeds window quotas; health checker evicts failing upstream replicas after two consecutive health check timeouts.

targets.method: Comparative load test measuring direct upstream response latency delta versus proxied path
targets.input: 2,000 requests per second across 200 concurrent HTTP client connections
targets.environment: Standard 4-core local CPU, Go 1.21+, local loopback interface
targets.minimum_pass: p99 latency overhead < 15ms under 1,000 requests per second
targets.target: p99 latency overhead < 8ms under 2,000 requests per second
targets.report: k6 benchmark summary report with percentile breakdown table

targets.method: Continuous client traffic benchmark while updating route rules via Admin API
targets.input: 10,000 consecutive HTTP GET requests sent during concurrent route table update
targets.minimum_pass: 10,000 of 10,000 requests return HTTP 200 status code
targets.target: 10,000 of 10,000 requests return HTTP 200 status code
targets.report: Test execution log verifying zero connection drops or 5xx server responses

targets.method: Automated chaos test terminating active upstream instance during sustained traffic load
targets.input: 500 requests per second background traffic across 3 simulated upstream instances
targets.environment: Local Docker bridge network with 3 mock upstream containers
targets.minimum_pass: Traffic convergence to healthy replicas within 3.0 seconds of upstream termination
targets.target: Traffic convergence to healthy replicas within 1.5 seconds of upstream termination
targets.report: Timestamped gateway error log and access metrics export

rubric.input: HTTP GET /api/users request through running gateway
rubric.action: Inspect response status code and headers
rubric.expected_result: Request proxies to mock upstream and returns HTTP 200 with X-Gateway-Proxy header
rubric.evidence_location: Terminal HTTP response headers and proxy console log
rubric.pass_criterion: Response status 200 OK received with gateway proxy header present

rubric.input: PUT request to /admin/routes registering /api/orders during active traffic
rubric.expected_result: New route takes effect immediately without restart and active requests continue without error
rubric.evidence_location: Admin API response payload and client traffic log
rubric.pass_criterion: 10,000 of 10,000 requests complete with HTTP 200 and zero connection resets

rubric.input: Burst of 20 rapid HTTP requests to route with 10 req/min limit
rubric.expected_result: First 10 requests succeed; 11th request receives HTTP 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After header
rubric.pass_criterion: HTTP status 429 returned on 11th request with valid Retry-After duration

rubric.input: Chaos signal sent to /chaos/kill terminating upstream replica 2
rubric.expected_result: Health checker detects failure and evicts node, routing subsequent traffic to healthy replicas
rubric.evidence_location: Gateway access log and Prometheus metric proxy_upstream_health_status
rubric.pass_criterion: Traffic rerouted within 3 seconds of termination with healthy replicas serving traffic

rubric.input: Dynamic random port and secret header token generated at runtime by verification script
rubric.expected_result: Test spawns fresh mock upstream, registers it dynamically via Admin API, and confirms response token validation
rubric.pass_criterion: Test passes with exit code 0 confirming dynamic proxy routing and header mutation

worksheet.q1: The student builds a high-performance reverse proxy and API Gateway in Go featuring an extensible middleware plugin chain, lock-free route table hot-reloading using atomic pointers, active health checking with weighted load balancing, and Prometheus metrics.
worksheet.q2: Core path: Go reverse proxy with tuned connection pooling, atomic route registry with Admin API, Auth and Rate Limiter plugins, active health balancer, and benchmark suite. Extended path: distributed Redis rate limiting, automatic ACME/TLS certificates, and WebAssembly plugin engine (+15h).
worksheet.q3: Components: Proxy Core Engine (8h), Atomic Route Registry (5h), Middleware Plugins (4h), Health Balancer (5h), Load Testing & Metrics (4h), Docs & Buffer (4h). Subtotal 30h x 1.15 = 35h.
worksheet.q4: Project types: API/backend, Systems/low-level/networking. Metrics built: Proxy Tail Latency Overhead, Hot-Reload Traffic Stability, Upstream Failover Convergence Duration. Rejected: multi-datacenter consensus latency (not building Raft cluster for edge proxy).
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: connection pooling and socket leaks, atomic lock-free hot reloading without race conditions, sync.Pool buffer recycling, and upstream health flapping mitigation.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: multi-instance mock upstream Go HTTP server exposing 10 synthetic endpoints with configurable delay and error injection. No real user data.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows WSL2, 8GB RAM, CPU only, $0 cost, zero cloud accounts. Fallback: run mock upstreams directly as background Go processes on localhost.
worksheet.q8: Riskiest component: TCP socket exhaustion during load test. Fallback: configure explicit HTTP keep-alive reuse and tune benchmark concurrency.
worksheet.q9: Potential faking: static Go server returning fake proxy headers. Anti-fake rubric item 5 creates a dynamic mock upstream on a random port at runtime and verifies proxy registration and token mutation.
worksheet.q10: Safety/ethics: Not required for local reverse proxy testing.
